_: Ballpark daily questions. APPEND-ONLY: day N (UTC days since 2026-10-01) is question N while the list is long enough, so never reorder or delete -- add new ones at the end.

questions.q: How many times does your heart beat in one day?
questions.h: About 70 beats a minute, times 60 minutes, times 24 hours: roughly 100,000.

questions.q: How many seconds are in a year?
questions.h: 60 seconds x 60 minutes x 24 hours x 365 days = 31,536,000. A handy shortcut: a year is about pi times ten million seconds.

questions.q: How far is the Moon from Earth?
questions.h: About 239,000 miles. Picture it as roughly 30 Earths, each about 8,000 miles wide, laid end to end.

questions.q: How many bones are in an adult human body?
questions.h: 206. Babies start with closer to 300; many fuse together as they grow.

questions.q: How many hairs are on a typical human head?
questions.h: The usual estimate is about 100,000. It varies a lot by hair colour and person.

questions.q: How long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.h: About 93 million miles divided by 186,000 miles per second: roughly 500 seconds, a bit over 8 minutes.

questions.q: How many chromosomes are in a typical human cell?
questions.h: 46, in 23 pairs: one set from each parent.

questions.q: How many cells make up a human body?
questions.h: A well-known 2013 estimate put it at about 37 trillion, give or take.

questions.q: How much water is in an Olympic swimming pool?
questions.h: 50 m long, 25 m wide, at least 2 m deep: 2,500 cubic meters, which is 2.5 million liters.

questions.q: How many words are in Moby-Dick?
questions.h: About 210,000. Think 600-odd pages at around 350 words a page.

questions.q: How many stars can you see with the naked eye on a dark, clear night?
questions.h: Roughly 2,500 at once from a truly dark site. City lights cut that to a few dozen.

questions.q: How far is it around the Earth at the equator?
questions.h: About 40,075 km. The meter was once defined so this would come out close to 40,000.

questions.q: How tall is the Eiffel Tower?
questions.h: About 330 meters, roughly the height of an 80-storey building.

questions.q: How many minutes are in an average human lifetime?
questions.h: 525,600 minutes a year times 79 years: about 41.5 million.

questions.q: How many Earths would fit inside the Sun?
questions.h: The Sun is about 109 Earths wide. Volume goes with the cube, so 109 x 109 x 109: roughly 1.3 million.

questions.q: How fast does light travel?
questions.h: About 300,000 km every second, fast enough to circle the Earth seven times in one second.

questions.q: How many steps does it take to walk a mile?
questions.h: A step is about 2.5 feet and a mile is 5,280 feet: roughly 2,100 steps.

questions.q: How many keys are on a standard computer keyboard?
questions.h: A full-size US keyboard has 104 keys; laptops usually drop to the high 70s or 80s.

questions.q: How far is the Earth from the Sun?
questions.h: About 150 million km, a distance so useful it has its own name: the astronomical unit.

questions.q: How many Earths would fit side by side across Jupiter?
questions.h: Jupiter is about 11 Earths wide.

questions.q: How far does light travel in one year?
questions.h: One light-year is about 9.46 trillion km: 300,000 km a second, for every second in a year.

questions.q: How far away is the nearest star after the Sun?
questions.h: Proxima Centauri, about 4.24 light-years away. Its light left it more than four years ago.

questions.q: How old is the universe?
questions.h: About 13.8 billion years.

questions.q: How old is the Earth?
questions.h: About 4.54 billion years, roughly a third the age of the universe.

questions.q: How wide is Mars?
questions.h: About 6,779 km, a little over half the width of Earth.

questions.q: How hot is the surface of the Sun?
questions.h: About 5,772 K, which is roughly 5,500 degrees Celsius.

questions.q: How long does moonlight take to reach Earth?
questions.h: About 1.3 seconds. Sunlight takes over eight minutes.

questions.q: How many Moons would fit inside the Earth?
questions.h: About 49. The Moon is roughly a quarter of Earth's width, and volume goes with the cube.

questions.q: How far is Pluto from the Sun, on average?
questions.h: About 5.9 billion km, around 39 times as far as Earth.

questions.q: How fast does the Earth travel around the Sun?
questions.h: About 107,000 km/h: nearly 30 km every second.

questions.q: How fast does sound travel through air?
questions.u: Meters per second, at room temperature
questions.h: About 343 m/s. Count the seconds between lightning and thunder and divide by three for kilometers.

questions.q: How many teeth does an adult have?
questions.h: 32, counting the four wisdom teeth.

questions.q: How many neurons are in a human brain?
questions.h: About 86 billion.

questions.q: How much blood is in an adult body?
questions.h: About 5 liters, roughly 7% of body weight.

questions.q: How many bones are in one human hand?
questions.h: 27: 8 in the wrist, 5 in the palm and 14 in the fingers.

questions.q: How tall is Mount Everest?
questions.h: 8,849 m, the 2020 joint China-Nepal survey figure.

questions.q: How deep is the deepest point in the ocean?
questions.h: The Challenger Deep is about 11,000 m down. Everest would fit in it with two kilometers to spare.

questions.q: How much surface area does the Earth have?
questions.h: About 510 million km2, around 71% of it ocean.

questions.q: How tall is the world's highest waterfall?
questions.h: Angel Falls in Venezuela drops 979 m.

questions.q: How big is the Pacific Ocean?
questions.h: About 165 million km2, more than all the land on Earth put together.

questions.q: How long is the Great Wall of China, counting all its branches?
questions.h: About 21,196 km, from a 2012 Chinese government survey.

questions.q: How deep is Lake Baikal, the world's deepest lake?
questions.h: 1,642 m at its deepest.

questions.q: How long is the Grand Canyon?
questions.h: About 446 km long.

questions.q: How big is the Sahara desert?
questions.h: About 9.2 million km2, close to the size of the United States.

questions.q: How tall is the Burj Khalifa?
questions.h: 828 m, the tallest building in the world since 2010.

questions.q: How tall was the Great Pyramid of Giza when it was built?
questions.h: About 146.6 m. It was the tallest structure humans had built for nearly 4,000 years.

questions.q: How long is the main span of the Golden Gate Bridge?
questions.h: 1,280 m between the two towers.

questions.q: How tall is the Statue of Liberty, from the ground to the torch?
questions.h: About 93 m including the pedestal; the statue alone is 46 m.

questions.q: How tall is the Empire State Building, to the tip of its antenna?
questions.h: About 443 m to the tip; 381 m to the roof.

questions.q: How wide is a Boeing 747-400, wingtip to wingtip?
questions.h: About 64.4 m, wider than the length of the Wright brothers' entire first flight (37 m).

questions.q: How many millimeters are in a mile?
questions.h: A mile is exactly 1,609.344 meters, so 1,609,344 mm.

questions.q: How many seconds are in a week?
questions.h: 7 x 24 x 60 x 60 = 604,800.

questions.q: How many US cups of water fit in a cubic meter?
questions.h: A cubic meter is 1,000 liters and a US cup is about 0.237 liters: about 4,227 cups.

questions.q: How many inches are in a kilometer?
questions.h: An inch is exactly 2.54 cm, so a kilometer is about 39,370 inches.

questions.q: How many hours are in a century?
questions.h: 365.25 days x 24 hours x 100 years: about 876,600.

questions.q: How many feet are in a nautical mile?
questions.h: A nautical mile is exactly 1,852 m: about 6,076 feet.

questions.q: How many US pennies, stacked flat, would reach a mile high?
questions.h: A penny is 1.52 mm thick and a mile is 1,609,344 mm: about 1.06 million pennies.

questions.q: How many keys are on a standard piano?
questions.h: 88: 52 white and 36 black.
